reason: The facts check out against the K2 code, but the finding adds nothing new, and its one new action should not be adopted. Verified in experiments/exp58_x138_safe_lowref/exp58-x138-safe-lowref.ipynb: KERNEL_START_TS is set in cell 0. All clips are predicted first. Then write_test_submission loops over sorted(predictions/*/unet_transformer/split_0/*.geff). The 9.5 h degrade is checked when each clip starts. safetail_divins_allowed is checked per clip just before the insertion, and a skip keeps the pre-insertion edges, which is exactly the twin graph for that clip (twin dummy: identical node rows, edges differ only at the 12 inserted / 5 stolen forks). Since elapsed <= runtime <= latency, 'clean' (L(K2) <= 8.0 h) does mean no gate fired on any clip, public or private. But this is already on record: step0.md (25 Sep 16:45) says 'alphabetical ... the LAST few clips' and 'public AND private in ONE run', R5H-1 in this same round says the same, and the READ TABLE CLEAN definition already says the insertion deadline never fired. The part that would change something is the action 'raise the runtime trigger only if both latencies point to a runtime above ~9 h'. That is a post-hoc loosening of the existing trigger (CONTEXT: L(K2) > 8.0 h -> raise to the user; READ TABLE row 5 / C5), and it is ambiguous. Read literally (the twin's own runtime > 9 h), it needs R(K2) of about 10.3-11 h, because the twin is 1.4-1.95 h faster at N <= 97 (52-72.5 s per clip of insertion: lab 2,907 s / 56 clips, step0 66 s, K2-vs-twin dummy repair 509 vs 219 s). That is past the 9.5 h degrade, so it would hide the only large-loss case. The '1.3 h' point value is also at the low end of the measured range. An alert costs nothing (any deadline move / D4 needs the user's OK anyway), so loosening it has no upside. Smaller point: 'never below the twin' holds only per clip. The aggregate still carries the insertion's own unknown private sign on the clips that were not skipped. The example 5% x 0.001 uses the public effect; the in-sample lab bound is +0.009-0.016. It stays a small loss either way (<~1e-3 even at 10% of clips). Feasibility: no code, byte-identical, nothing to build. Value: about 0.
fix: Do not change the trigger. Keep 'L(K2) > 8.0 h -> raise to the user' and READ TABLE row 5 / C5 exactly as written. At score time (round 4, A4), add one information-only line: 'clean also covers private (one hidden run); not clean costs at most K2 -> twin on the last-sorted clips (8.0 h gate), plus a degrade only if R(K2) > 9.5 h'. If a sharper runtime read is wanted, use R(K2) <= min(L(K2), L(twin) + D_max) with D_max = 1.95 h (97 clips x 72.5 s). Mention a deadline move / D4 to the user only if that bound is > 9.0 h. Never use the 1.3 h point value in a bound.
realistic_gain: ~0 score. At most a clearer score-time note. Adopting the proposed trigger change has a small negative expected value (it could hide a real 9.5 h tail degrade on a private embryo).
